items.title: Podcasts By Dr. Kirk Adams: Interview with Rachel Antoine, Senior Director of International Operations, Braille Institute
items.description:
In this warm and wide-ranging episode of Podcasts by Dr. Kirk Adams, Kirk welcomes Rachel Antoine, Senior Director of International Operations at Braille Institute, for a conversation about Braille literacy and the programs that sustain it. Kirk opens with his own Braille history, losing his sight at five, learning to read and write Braille from Mrs. Summers at the Oregon State School for the Blind, and depending on Braille books through long hospital stays, then traces his three encounters with Braille Challenge: a regional in Tampa, a 2019 keynote at the Braille Challenge gala, and a return visit in 2026 where he met Rachel. Rachel explains that Braille Challenge has grown from one Southern California regional in 2000 to over 80 regionals worldwide, reaching around 2,200 students a year and over 26,000 since it began, with the competition as the vehicle and Braille literacy as the mission.

items.title: When Disclosure Costs You the Interview: Seattle’s Disability:IN Chapter Takes on the Question I Lived
items.description:
Here, Dr. Kirk Adams tells the story of the impossible choice that shaped his career. In 1983, fresh out of Whitman College with a degree in economics, he could either say nothing about his blindness and watch an interview collapse the moment he walked in with a long white cane, or disclose it at the top of his cover letter and stop getting phone interviews altogether. Two bad options, and no third one on offer. He connects that experience directly to "The Courage to Be Human at Work: Vulnerability, Access, and Connection," a free 90-minute webinar hosted by Disability:IN Washington on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, and led by Linea Johnson, Founder and CEO of The Thrive Shift. Its central question, he writes, is one he recognized on sight: how do we create workplaces where people don't have to choose between protecting themselves and belonging?

items.title: Another Door to Knock On: Jennifer Bazer and the Palmetto Council of the Blind
items.description:
Here, Dr. Kirk Adams introduces Jennifer Bazer, President of the Palmetto Council of the Blind of South Carolina and a newly elected member of the Board of Directors of the American Council of the Blind, and makes the case for supporting the Council's Kicking for a Cause online auction, which closes on September 20, 2026. Blind since birth, a social worker by training and a veteran of more than a decade managing large federal workforce programs, Bazer founded the Palmetto Council in 2023 with a deliberately simple aim: to give a newly blind South Carolinian, a family member who does not know where to turn, or anyone looking for a way in "another door they could knock on."

The post Another Door to Knock On: Jennifer Bazer and the Palmetto Council of the Blind appeared first on Dr. Kirk Adams.

items.title: What We Inherit — and What We Must Build Next
items.description: Here, Dr. Kirk Adams reflects on launching the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion on September 1, in a span of days that also brought the deaths of Dolly Parton, Wendell Berry, and Gloria Steinem. He writes candidly about his discomfort at honoring three white figures in a piece about a coalition devoted to diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and belonging, and he insists that the long struggle for freedom has been led, sustained, and repeatedly rescued by Black people, Indigenous people, people of color, women, LGBTQ+ people, people with disabilities, immigrants, workers, and countless others whose names never reach a history book. items.title: Recording: Official Launch of The Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion
items.description:
Here, Dr. Kirk Adams shares the full recording of the September 1, 2026 public launch of the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion, the national membership community created by the Institute for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion to help people working in diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility and belonging move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power.

The post Recording: Official Launch of The Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion appeared first on Dr. Kirk Adams.

items.title: The Doors Are Open: How to Join the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion
items.description: Here, Dr. Kirk Adams announces that the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion went live on September 1, 2026, opened not with a webinar or a panel but with an "Ask Us Anything" hour of questions, frustrations, ideas and lived experience. He explains what the Coalition actually is: a way for members to move from reactive, isolated survival mode to strategic, sustainable, collective power, built on four words, Connect, Learn, Act, Together. He is direct about who it is for, which is everybody, and equally direct that disability inclusion and accessibility are not a side room in it but a dedicated space by design. items.title: This Is Our Season: Join Us September 1st  When We Launch, Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity & Inclusion
items.description: Here, Dr. Kirk Adams invites readers to the free virtual launch of the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion on Tuesday, September 1st, 11:00 a.m. to noon Pacific / 2:00 to 3:00 p.m. Eastern. Writing as Executive Director of The Institute for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion, he opens on the turning of the season and uses it to name a harder truth: across workplaces, schools, nonprofits, government agencies and communities, champions of diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, belonging and human dignity are watching programs dismantled, funding disappear and language censored, and are doing that work feeling like the only one in the room. That isolation, he argues, is not merely painful but strategically costly, because the forces working against inclusion win when advocates are exhausted, fragmented and afraid. items.title: RESIST! We Have Inherited a Legacy. Now It Is Our Turn.
items.description:
Here, Dr. Kirk Adams invites readers to the free livestreamed launch of the Community Coalition for Sustainable Diversity and Inclusion on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, from 11:00 a.m. to noon Pacific (2:00 to 3:00 p.m. Eastern), and argues that the Coalition is inheriting a legacy rather than inventing one. Writing from a visit to Oakland in the Black Panther Party's sixtieth anniversary year, he looks past the iconography to the Party's Community Survival Programs, the free breakfasts, health clinics, sickle-cell testing, legal services and support for seniors and disabled people, and draws out the line that anchors the piece: resistance isn't only about what we stand against, it is about what we build together.

The post RESIST! We Have Inherited a Legacy. Now It Is Our Turn. appeared first on Dr. Kirk Adams.
